title: Grid-Scale Battery Storage Investment
prompt: Your client is a regional electric utility deciding whether to build a 100 MW / 400 MWh grid-scale battery (a 4-hour battery). It would charge when power is cheap, discharge when power is expensive, and earn capacity and grid-service payments. Should they build it?
background: The client is a regulated utility with its own grid access and a low cost of capital.
The battery arbitrages power prices (charge low, discharge high) and is paid for being available (capacity) and for grid services.
Battery useful life is about 10–15 years.
The client will build and own it, not partner.

clarifying_answers.What is the goal: A positive-NPV investment over the battery's life, and strategic positioning for a grid with more renewables.
clarifying_answers.What size: 100 MW of power, 400 MWh of energy — it can discharge its full 400 MWh over 4 hours, roughly once per day.
clarifying_answers.Regulatory stance: The regulator is supportive of storage.

exhibits.name: Capex and Revenue Streams
exhibits.description: Build cost and the three revenue streams.
exhibits.data: Capex: $300 per kWh x 400,000 kWh = $120M. Revenue: (1) energy arbitrage at a $60/MWh spread, discharging 400 MWh/day for ~350 days/year; (2) capacity payments of $80 per kW-year on 100,000 kW; (3) grid-service payments of about $2M/year.

exhibits.name: Operating Costs
exhibits.data: Operating costs (O&M, round-trip efficiency losses, insurance) total about $4M per year.

good_framework: Value of the asset: the three revenue streams (arbitrage, capacity, grid services) minus opex, vs. the capex.
Economics: annual net cash flow, simple payback, and whether it clears within the 10–15 year life.
Right to win: the utility's grid access, low cost of capital, regulatory support.
Risks: price-spread volatility, capacity-market rule changes, battery degradation.
Decision tied to the positive-NPV goal.

quant.question: What is the annual energy-arbitrage revenue?
quant.work: 400 MWh/day x 350 days = 140,000 MWh; x $60/MWh spread = $8.4M/year.

quant.question: What is the total annual net cash flow?
quant.work: Arbitrage $8.4M + capacity (100,000 kW x $80 = $8M) + grid services $2M = $18.4M revenue; minus $4M opex = $14.4M.

quant.question: What is the simple payback on the $120M capex?
quant.work: $120M / $14.4M per year = ~8.3 years, within the 10–15 year life.

recommendation: Build it. Net cash flow of ~$14.4M/year gives an ~8.3-year payback inside a 10–15 year life, and the utility has a real right to win (grid access, low cost of capital, regulatory support). Key risks are price-spread volatility and capacity-market rule changes, so hedge where possible and stress-test the spread. Recommend proceeding, ideally phased, with a downside case on the arbitrage spread.
